white: Construct two otherwise valid expenses with titles of 60 and 61 characters. Expect success at 60 and a title-field error at 61.
Exercises both sides of the title-length guard after the nonempty-title check.
Use 100,000,000 cents and 100,000,001 cents, with shares that sum to each total. Accept the first; reject the second with the maximum-amount message.
Exercises the inclusive upper amount boundary while keeping the preceding title and positive-amount guards valid.
Use Alice 250 cents, Alice 250 cents, Bob 500 cents for a 1,000-cent expense. Expect the duplicate-participant error.
The second Alice executes the false branch of seen.add; a matching total prevents an unrelated sum error from masking this check.
Use Alice -1 cent and Bob 1,001 cents for a 1,000-cent expense. Expect the negative-share error.
Membership checks pass, so execution reaches the negative-share branch; the total still matches.
Use notes of 300 and 301 characters with valid title, amount, membership, and shares. Accept 300; reject 301 with the note-field error.
Reaches the final validateNote call after every preceding expense guard succeeds.
Negative percentage hidden by a matching total
Use -1,000 and 11,000 basis points (-10% and 110%), with nonnegative shares totaling 1,000 cents. Expect the negative-percentage error.
Exercises the new per-share negative-percentage guard; a total of 100% alone is insufficient.
D1: Failed before the fix because the expense was accepted. Fixed by rejecting negative per-share basis points in InputValidator.validateExpense. Passes after the fix.
Use 2,147,483,647, 2,147,483,647, and 10,002 basis points for three distinct group members. Shares total 1,000 cents. Expect rejection showing 42949772.96%, not 100%.
The mathematical sum is 4,294,977,296; a 32-bit integer wraps it to 10,000. This targets the accumulator's overflow boundary.
D2: Failed before the fix because the expense was accepted. Fixed by using a long accumulator and exact decimal formatting. Passes after the fix.
Use Alice 100% / 1,000 cents and Bob 0% / 0 cents. Expect acceptance.
Exercises the successful percentage path and ensures the negative-value fix preserves the allowed zero boundary.
No new defect; protects against an over-restrictive fix.
Percentage and monetary totals are independent
Use 50% / 499 cents and 50% / 500 cents against a 1,000-cent total. Expect: Amounts add up to $9.99, not $10.00.
Passes percentage validation, then takes the monetary-sum mismatch branch.
Construct a positive 1,000-cent expense with an empty share list. Expect the payer-must-be-a-participant error.
Skips the participant loop and takes the missing-payer branch before sum validation.
